description: The `OrderPlaced` record shared by the API and the worker, which defines what a message carries and changes only in backward-compatible ways.
The producer-assigned id stored with the order and set on every publish, which the consumer uses as its deduplication key.
A RabbitMQ policy that sets `delivery-limit` and `dead-letter-exchange` on the quorum queue, so failing messages move to the dead-letter queue after a fixed number of attempts.
In RabbitMQ 4.3 and later, `BasicRejectAsync` counts towards a quorum queue's delivery limit and `BasicNackAsync` does not.
The number of unacknowledged messages RabbitMQ sends to one consumer at a time, set with `BasicQosAsync`, which bounds in-flight work per worker.
A GUID created by a scoped service and logged for each message, which proves that every message gets its own DI scope and `DbContext`.
